coachingPoints: Start every workout with screening technique — it is the power forward's signature skill.
Track screen assists and box-outs, not just points, to reward the real job.
Build the pick-and-pop three before the roll game; shooting creates the roll.
Drill short-roll passing: catch at the free-throw line and find the corner in one beat.
commonMistakes: Slipping every screen instead of making real contact — no contact, no advantage.
Camping in the paint on offense and killing spacing.
Chasing blocks instead of staying down and contesting vertically.
Refusing to shoot open threes, letting the defender sag into the paint.
description: Power forward development: screening, rolling and popping, rebounding, interior defense and stretch-four shooting.
gameSituations: Pick & roll — setting the screen, then rolling hard or popping to the arc.
Offensive rebound — crashing from the weak side for putbacks.
Switch defense — containing a guard on the perimeter for two dribbles.
Late game — securing the defensive rebound that seals the win.

howTo.detail: Set wide, legal, angled screens: sprint to the spot, stop with a wide base, hands protecting, and hold for a one-count. Then roll hard to the rim with hands ready, or pop to space if your defender helps.
howTo.title: Screen, roll, and pop

howTo.detail: Become a reliable catch-and-shoot threat from the top and the wings. A power forward who shoots 35%+ from three is a 'stretch four' — their defender cannot help inside, which opens the paint for everyone.
howTo.title: Stretch the floor

howTo.detail: Own both backboards: seal your player with a forearm, pursue the ball with two hands, and outlet quickly. Offensive rebounding from the weak side creates the easiest points in basketball.
howTo.title: Rebound everything

howTo.detail: Guard the paint first: be the low man in rotations, tag rollers, and contest vertically at the rim. Then develop the ability to switch onto smaller players for short stretches.
howTo.title: Anchor the interior defense

howTo.detail: Catch on the move, finish with either hand, and use the drop step, jump hook, and up-and-under against single coverage. Keep moves to two dribbles or fewer.
howTo.title: Finish inside efficiently

howTo.detail: From the short roll or the high post, read the defense and hit cutters and corner shooters. Modern power forwards are playmakers, not just finishers.
howTo.title: Pass from the elbows

title: Power Forward Development
whatIsIt: The power forward — the '4' — is the team's interior engine: setting the screens that free teammates, rolling to the rim or popping for threes, rebounding on both ends, and anchoring help defense. They do the physical work that makes everyone else's job easier.

The modern '4' has split into two styles: the traditional banger who lives in the paint, and the 'stretch four' who shoots threes and pulls opposing bigs away from the basket. The best power forwards blend both.
whyItMatters: Screens and rebounds do not make highlight reels, but they win games. A power forward who screens with contact creates open shots every possession; one who rebounds ends opponent possessions and starts fast breaks. It is the ultimate winning position — the work is unglamorous, and the impact is enormous.
